name: US dollar
summary: Dollar index 103.8 on 20 Nov, near its 52-week high and about 5% higher over three months, at the Watch line
state: The DXY dollar index closed near 103.8 on 20 Nov, a fraction below its 52-week high and about 5.0% higher over three months, at the 5% Watch line (Yahoo Finance). The level is inside the 90–108 range, and SOFR stayed within 3bp of the Fed's reserve rate over five days (FRED), so no dollar funding stress is visible.
for_you: A stronger dollar raises the cost of dollar-priced imports and of dollar debt for borrowers outside the US. Travellers to the US get less for their pounds or euros.
rubric_hit: DXY 3m move 4.72% has not yet cleared the 4.5% exit line, so Watch holds
why: The dollar is the world's funding currency; violent moves squeeze emerging markets and anyone with dollar debts.
drivers: Fed vs other central banks, safe-haven demand, trade policy, reserve diversification.

rubric.alert: DXY moved > 8% in 3 months, or dollar funding stress (Fed swap lines drawn materially).
rubric.watch: DXY moved 5–8% in 3 months, or outside 90–108.
rubric.normal: DXY moved < 5% over 3 months and is between 90 and 108.
